evidence_packet.evidence_text: Three people injured in Moston police vehicle crash - BBC News Image source, Dave Thompson/PA Wire Image caption, The incident happened on St Mary's Road, Moston, at about 10:35 BST on Tuesday, police said By Angela Ferguson North West Published 22 minutes ago Three people including two police officers have been injured in a crash involving a car and a police vehicle responding to an emergency incident. The crash happened on St Mary's Road in Moston, Manchester, at about 10:35 BST on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. A GMP spokesperson said the driver of the car and two officers from the police vehicle sustained injuries and were taken to hospital as a precautionary measure. "At this stage, the injuries are not believed to be life-threatening," they added. GMP said a scene remained in place while their work continued and they thanked members of the public for their patience as this was carried out. title: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens

evidence_packet.title: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens
evidence_packet.lead: A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham
evidence_packet.summary: A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Targeting bin crews and traffic wardens out doing their jobs is "unacceptable", a council has said, after a wagon had a brick thrown through its window while out on its rounds. At least one traffic warden was also said to have been targeted in the Goldwick area, Oldham Council said. Speaking after the bin wagon incident last month, a spokesperson said the wagon had its driver-side window smashed "by a resident" and a parking enforcement officer was subjected to abuse. "Our staff are working hard every day to deliver essential services for communities across the borough. These unacceptable actions not only put people at risk but also delay services for other residents," they added. The council has recently laid fresh double yellow lines and given out 273 parking fines so far this year in parts of the Waterloo Street area. "Enforcement officers are carrying out their duties to help keep our highways safe and accessible," the council continued. "Any form of verbal or physical abuse towards our staff is completely unacceptable and will not be tolerated." evidence_packet.title: I hope Oasis reunion film encourages families to make up, says writer
evidence_packet.lead: Steven Knight says the Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger film was "incredibly emotional"
evidence_packet.summary: Steven Knight says the Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger film was "incredibly emotional"
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The creator and writer of a film documenting last year's Oasis reunion tour has said he hoped it would encourage others to resolve family feuds like the Gallagher brothers Steven Knight said Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger - which charts their emotional reconciliation after 15 years - was "incredibly emotional" and had resonated with many people The Peaky Blinders writer said the reaction to the candid film - which shows "real emotions from real people" - had been "extraordinary", adding: "When you write fiction you aspire to having these kind of reactions." He said if it inspired people to get in touch with family members they have not spoken to for years "then I'm all for it - it's great" The project is part concert film and part documentary and charts the Manchester band on their reunion world tour, which kicked off in Cardiff in July last year It also features the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years

title: Papyrus suicide prevention charity in administration

evidence_packet.title: Papyrus suicide prevention charity in administration
evidence_packet.lead: The 3 Dads Walking, who raised £1.5m for Papyrus, say it is "very difficult to accept" its closure
evidence_packet.summary: The 3 Dads Walking, who raised £1.5m for Papyrus, say it is "very difficult to accept" its closure
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A suicide prevention charity, which received more than £1.5m of funding from the 3 Dads Walking group, has gone into administration Opus Restructuring and Insolvency said its appointment as administrators for Papyrus Prevention of Young Suicide had followed an "extended and extremely difficult period" for the charity The 3 Dads Walking, Andy Airey from Cumbria, Mike Palmer from Greater Manchester and Tim Owen from Norfolk, each lost a daughter – Sophie, Beth and Emily - to suicide. They said they found it "very difficult to accept" Papyrus was closing Chair of Papyrus trustees Harry Biggs-Davison said: "It has been almost unbearable for us trustees to have had to make the decision." Biggs-Davison, who lost his 25-year-old son Patrick to suicide, in 2015 said he took pride "in the certainty that our charity has saved and offered hope to countless young lives during the past 30 years" But he added: "After nearly two years of struggling to keep the charity alive in such a difficult financial climate, we have had to accept that we have no alternative."

title: Steve Coogan on Warwick Mill deal and Middleton regeneration

evidence_packet.title: Steve Coogan on Warwick Mill deal and Middleton regeneration
evidence_packet.lead: The actor says local people should help shape the regeneration of his hometown
evidence_packet.summary: The actor says local people should help shape the regeneration of his hometown
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Steve Coogan on Warwick Mill deal and Middleton regeneration - BBC News Image caption, Rose Marley and Steve Coogan are set to head up the mayoral development corporation By Kevin Fitzpatrick North West , Reporting from in Middleton Published 8 September 2026 Comedian Steve Coogan says a deal to acquire an historic cotton mill could "lead on to great things" as he helped lead regeneration plans in his hometown of Middleton, in Greater Manchester. Rochdale Borough Council said it had struck a deal to acquire Grade II-listed Warwick Mill, vacant for at least a decade, after a consultation of more than 2,000 people. The Bafta-winning actor co-chairs the shadow board setting up Middleton's proposed mayoral development corporation (MDC), which would have powers to buy land and drive development. At Middleton Arena, Coogan said residents should be involved "from the ground up", with regeneration done "with people, not to them". Coogan said Middleton wanted to build on the regeneration model used in Stockport , but "do things a bit differently here". He said consultation should involve people "from the ground up so that people feel involved". "We're doing things with people, not to them," he said. Image source, Rochdale Borough Council Image caption, The Grade II listed building stopped operating as a cotton mill in 1965 and has been vacant for at least a decade Warwick Mill was built in 1907, stopped operating as a cotton mill in 1965 and has been vacant for at least 10 years. Coogan described the building as an "eyesore", but said bringing it back into use could demonstrate that regeneration was happening. "If you can turn that around, then it's a sign and a signifier to people that things are actually moving," he said. "I think it's going to lead on to great things." Image

title: A&E did not get the basics right - now my son's life is ruined at 32

evidence_packet.title: A&E did not get the basics right - now my son's life is ruined at 32
evidence_packet.lead: Oli's experience is one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England, BBC analysis shows
evidence_packet.summary: Oli's experience is one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England, BBC analysis shows
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health correspondent Published 8 September 2026 In May 2024, a few months after having treatment for a brain tumour, Oli Coppock went to Warrington Hospital's emergency department with bad headaches and dizziness He underwent tests and assessments, but did not have a brain scan, before going home. It was a decision that ultimately ruined his life at the age of 32, his family says. A week later, with fluid building up on the brain, he suffered a cardiac arrest. He did not recover and now l Oli's case is just one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England relating to A&E care. An analysis by the BBC shows there has been a 41% rise in cases over the past five years, with doctors linking it to the long delays and pressures being seen in em Oli's father, Stephen, says he knows A&E staff are under pressure, but he cannot understand how a brain scan was not ordered, given his son's medical history Despite the brain tumour and a recent diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, Oli was otherwise fit and well and positive about his future. He had a career in digital marketing, loved going to the gym and did some DJing in his spare time Stephen says the whole family – including Oli's six siblings - has been left "angry and broken" by what happened to him

title: Garry Bridges sets out priorities as Manchester council leader

evidence_packet.title: Garry Bridges sets out priorities as Manchester council leader
evidence_packet.lead: Garry Bridges also discussed rough sleeping, high-rise development and the city's G20 hopes
evidence_packet.summary: Garry Bridges also discussed rough sleeping, high-rise development and the city's G20 hopes
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester's new council leader has said delivering more homes is an "absolute priority" as he set out his ambitions for the city Garry Bridges told BBC Radio Manchester's Joe McGrath Breakfast Show that high-rise developments had a place in Manchester's housing mix, but were not affordable to everyone The council aims to help deliver 36,000 homes by 2032, including at least 10,000 social, council or genuinely affordable homes. The council said almost a quarter of the affordable homes target had already been met Bridges also described rough sleeping as a "complete failure of the state and of society", with the council expecting about £2m through the government's £442m Rough Sleeping Programme Bridges, who was formally appointed council leader last week after succeeding Bev Craig, said getting the job had taken "a good few days to sink in" He described it as an "amazing honour" and said becoming leader was not something he had imagined when he first became involved in politics

title: The Guest List play festivals but still rehearse in a garage

evidence_packet.title: The Guest List play festivals but still rehearse in a garage
evidence_packet.lead: The band are in their early 20s but have played major festivals and even dates in Japan
evidence_packet.summary: The band are in their early 20s but have played major festivals and even dates in Japan
evidence_packet.evidence_text: They are all in their early 20s and practise in one of their parents' garages, but Greater Manchester band The Guest List have spent the year playing gigs in front of thousands of people From playing Neighbourhood in Warrington, to festivals in Japan and then Reading and Leeds over the bank holiday weekend, the band have performed on a number of large stages And they say being from Greater Manchester, has a huge impact on them - as does the area's musical heritage "Because of that heritage, the underground scene is still very active and healthy which has been a massive help for us coming through," said vocalist Cai Alty Four of the five members of the band - Alty, guitarists Leio Hunter and Tom Quigley, and drummer Angus Gilchrist, met at school in Altrincham while playing in the school's swing band, with bassist Sid Wallace joining them later Alty said the band had grown up listening to Manchester bands, in particular The Stone Roses who went to the same school

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A suicide prevention charity, which received more than £1.5m of funding from the 3 Dads Walking group, has gone into administration Opus Restructuring and Insolvency said its appointment as administrators for Papyrus Prevention of Young Suicide had followed an "extended and extremely difficult period" for the charity The 3 Dads Walking, Andy Airey from Cumbria, Mike Palmer from Greater Manchester and Tim Owen from Norfolk, each lost a daughter – Sophie, Beth and Emily - to suicide. They said they found it "very difficult to accept" Papyrus was closing Chair of Papyrus trustees Harry Biggs-Davison said: "It has been almost unbearable for us trustees to have had to make the decision." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Health correspondent Published 8 September 2026 In May 2024, a few months after having treatment for a brain tumour, Oli Coppock went to Warrington Hospital's emergency department with bad headaches and dizziness He underwent tests and assessments, but did not have a brain scan, before going home. It was a decision that ultimately ruined his life at the age of 32, his family says. A week later, with fluid building up on the brain, he suffered a cardiac arrest. He did not recover and now l Oli's case is just one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England relating to A&E care. An analysis by the BBC shows there has been a 41% rise in cases over the past five years, with doctors linking it to the long delays and pressures being seen in em Oli's father, Stephen, says he knows A&E staff are under pressure, but he cannot understand how a brain scan was not ordered, given his son's medical history Despite the brain tumour and a recent diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, Oli was otherwise fit and well and positive about his future. He had a career in digital marketing, loved going to the gym and did some DJing in his spare time Stephen says the whole family – including Oli's six siblings - has been left "angry and broken" by what happened to him

evidence_packet.evidence_text: For children starting a new secondary school this year social media means they will likely always have a way of keeping in touch with friends after they leave But for past generations it was very different. Often the last day of school was the last time you saw most class mates - even if you might not realise it at the time It was something that prompted grandmother Karen Feay to track down the people she started Rivington & Blackrod Grammar School in Bolton with 60 years ago "I bumped into an old school friend and we got talking about our school memories - and it snowballed from there," she said. "We all started in 1966 which makes everyone 70 or 71 years old now." evidence_packet.evidence_text: She was there for the first official screening of Don’t Look Back In Anger - the Steven Knight documentary which charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s epic reunion tour . And as she explains in this review and this video synopsis , the film is an “unapologetically uplifting” film It features footage from rehearsals, backstage and onstage moments and the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years. And it’s these candid moments that are the most impactful and tear-jerking The film explores the profound emotional impact of the tour and what the band's music means to audiences and generations worldwide. But as Jenna explains, it was a little surreal to see two lads from Burnage walking the same red carpet as George Clooney, Orlando Bloom and Amanda Not that she got to enjoy too much glamour . After speedily writing up her review, she was forced to use a sandy beach bar toilet to put on her dress and heels for the premiere, while a colleague was forced to get changed behind an industrial sized bin. You can take the girl out The film, and its Manchester stars, received a eight-minute standing ovation. And Jenna reports that Noel even looked to be wiping tears away as Liam gleefully hyped up the crowd who were cheering them on She describes the film as “a story about friendships mended, bonds built, forgiveness over ego and the power of music”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury The Bury multi-storey car park that could 80 new homes built on top of it Plans have been in the offing since 2009 Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:24, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Q-Park, in Knowsley Street, Bury (Image: Google) A multi-storey car park in Bury town centre could see almost 80 new homes built on top of it The one-acre Q-Park site, in Knowsley Street, opposite the town hall, has long been earmarked for housing . Currently home to a 404-space underground car park, the structure was built to take the weight of an additional six-storey building above it However, the space above has remained vacant since the below-ground project was completed in 2009. Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Garry Bridges has friends in high places. His old boss, Bev Craig, has just been elected as Greater Manchester mayor. And the man who used to hold her position, Andy Burnham , is now Prime Minister Coun Bridges hopes these two powerful Labour figures can help him to carry out his ambitions as the new leader of Manchester Council. “We want to make sure that Manchester is right at the front of the queue,” he told local democracy reporter Declan Carey in his first interview in After a vote in the chamber on Thursday night, Coun Bridges has taken control of a £1bn budget. He has also taken on Manchester’s housing crisis and a stark rough sleeping problem Though he steps up at a challenging time, he insists it’s also a time of tremendous opportunity View 3 Images New Manchester City Council Leader Garry Bridges (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former council estate kid who grew up in the Black Country, Coun Bridges came to Manchester for university in 2005 and never left. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police release CCTV after 70,000 pints of Guinness stolen in Cheshire Nearly 900 barrels of stout still missing News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 17:26, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:07, 08 Sep 2026 View 6 Images Police would like to speak to this man after 7 Images of two people want to speak to after an incident in which 70,000 pints of Guinness were stolen have been released by police. The two men were captured on CCTV as they arrived at industrial park in Cheshire Footage shows the pair getting out of HGV cabs and speaking to a security guard to ask for a barrier to be lifted. Police believe the lorries were those used to hook up to two trailers containing the stout worth £115,000 Both men arrived at a depot in Runcorn but about two hours apart. On August 31st police were alerted that two HGV trailers containing about 880 barrels of Guinness had been stolen Diageo, which owns Guinness, has a packaging warehouse on the Whitehouse Industrial Estate on Aston Lane View 6 Images Police would like to speak to this man after 70,000 pints of Guinness were stilen from an industrial estate in Cheshire

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton A blueprint for the future of Middleton, and not a £6 oat milk latte in sight “In places like Middleton, the next 10 years can be a good 10 years. We are not accepting decline" View 8 Images "People are proud to be from Middleton" Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:21, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:13, 08 Sep 2026 Middleton is changing, but the signs of its regeneration won’t be reduced to a ‘£6 oat milk latte’, according to Bev Craig At the Rochdale town’s arena last night (September 7), a different vision was laid out. Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: National news Portsmouth migrant protestors face backlash after RNLI lifeboat rescuers branded 'traitors' 'Common sense and decency have gone out the window' Comments News Tom Pettifor , Paul Britton Reporter and Jeremy Armstrong 07:00, 08 Sep 2026 Vi Protestors in Portsmouth are facing an angry backlash after branding lifeboat heroes 'traitors' for rescuing a boat carrying asylum seekers in the Channel A group confronted Royal National Lifeboat Institute crews on Sunday night. The crews, who were based on the Isle of Wight, helped a 'mega dinghy' carrying around 120 people which was stranded in the Channel It came into UK waters from Cherbourg, near the ferry crossing for Portsmouth, rather than using the usual route from Calais into Dover, Kent. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury The Bury multi-storey car park that could 80 new homes built on top of it Plans have been in the offing since 2009 Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:24, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Q-Park, in Knowsley Street, Bury (Image: Google) A multi-storey car park in Bury town centre could see almost 80 new homes built on top of it The one-acre Q-Park site, in Knowsley Street, opposite the town hall, has long been earmarked for housing . Currently home to a 404-space underground car park, the structure was built to take the weight of an additional six-storey building above it However, the space above has remained vacant since the below-ground project was completed in 2009. Bury council has said the land ‘regularly attracts anti-social behaviour ’ and its current appearance is ‘detrimental to the wider street scheme’ The authority now wants to see new homes delivered on the site. Expectations are that around 77 flats could be built there Town hall bosses are proposing to dispose of the site to Watson Construction Ltd which was selected for the project through a tendering process. Watson Construction are also expected to take on the nearby project at Pyramid Park which could see around 138 homes built on it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Garry Bridges has friends in high places. His old boss, Bev Craig, has just been elected as Greater Manchester mayor. And the man who used to hold her position, Andy Burnham , is now Prime Minister Coun Bridges hopes these two powerful Labour figures can help him to carry out his ambitions as the new leader of Manchester Council. “We want to make sure that Manchester is right at the front of the queue,” he told local democracy reporter Declan Carey in his first interview in After a vote in the chamber on Thursday night, Coun Bridges has taken control of a £1bn budget. He has also taken on Manchester’s housing crisis and a stark rough sleeping problem Though he steps up at a challenging time, he insists it’s also a time of tremendous opportunity View 3 Images New Manchester City Council Leader Garry Bridges (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former council estate kid who grew up in the Black Country, Coun Bridges came to Manchester for university in 2005 and never left. We are not accepting decline" View 8 Images "People are proud to be from Middleton" Comments News George Lythgoe Local Demo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Middleton A blueprint for the future of Middleton, and not a £6 oat milk latte in sight “In places like Middleton, the next 10 years can be a good 10 years. We are not accepting decline" View 8 Images "People are proud to be from Middleton" Comments News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 17:21, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:13, 08 Sep 2026 Middleton is changing, but the signs of its regeneration won’t be reduced to a ‘£6 oat milk latte’, according to Bev Craig At the Rochdale town’s arena last night (September 7), a different vision was laid out. Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police release CCTV after 70,000 pints of Guinness stolen in Cheshire Nearly 900 barrels of stout still missing News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 17:26, 08 Sep 2026 Updated 18:07, 08 Sep 2026 View 6 Images Police would like to speak to this man after 7 Images of two people want to speak to after an incident in which 70,000 pints of Guinness were stolen have been released by police. The two men were captured on CCTV as they arrived at industrial park in Cheshire Footage shows the pair getting out of HGV cabs and speaking to a security guard to ask for a barrier to be lifted. Police believe the lorries were those used to hook up to two trailers containing the stout worth £115,000 Both men arrived at a depot in Runcorn but about two hours apart. On August 31st police were alerted that two HGV trailers containing about 880 barrels of Guinness had been stolen Diageo, which owns Guinness, has a packaging warehouse on the Whitehouse Industrial Estate on Aston Lane View 6 Images Police would like to speak to this man after 70,000 pints of Guinness were stilen from an industrial estate in Cheshire

evidence_packet.evidence_text: She was there for the first official screening of Don’t Look Back In Anger - the Steven Knight documentary which charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s epic reunion tour . And as she explains in this review and this video synopsis , the film is an “unapologetically uplifting” film It features footage from rehearsals, backstage and onstage moments and the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years. And it’s these candid moments that are the most impactful and tear-jerking The film explores the profound emotional impact of the tour and what the band's music means to audiences and generations worldwide. But as Jenna explains, it was a little surreal to see two lads from Burnage walking the same red carpet as George Clooney, Orlando Bloom and Amanda Not that she got to enjoy too much glamour . After speedily writing up her review, she was forced to use a sandy beach bar toilet to put on her dress and heels for the premiere, while a colleague was forced to get changed behind an industrial sized bin. You can take the girl out The film, and its Manchester stars, received a eight-minute standing ovation. And Jenna reports that Noel even looked to be wiping tears away as Liam gleefully hyped up the crowd who were cheering them on She describes the film as “a story about friendships mended, bonds built, forgiveness over ego and the power of music”

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

It’s played exclusively in doubles, on a 10x20m court enclosed by four walls. In the last three years, padel in Manchester has exploded in popularity. The site lies to the north of Dobbinetts Lane, between Brooks Drive and existing homes, and south-west of Wythenshawe Hospital. It forms part of the much larger Davenport Green area – previously known as Timperley Wedge – which has been allocated for development under the Greater Manchester Places for Everyone plan. That wider allocation envisages thousands of new homes alongside employment space, community facilities, green space and new transport infrastructure. A visual showing the proposed housing plan off Dobbinetts Lane Prospect Homes has revealed that an earlier version of its Dobbinetts Lane development contained 179 homes. evidence_packet.summary: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 12 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 12 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council Fiona has enjoyed a distinguished career in local government law and public service, first qualifying as a solicitor in 1985 She has held range of senior leadership positions across local government, including roles at Stoke-on-Trent City Council, the London Borough of Brent, the Greater London Authority and the London Borough of Sutton Fiona joined Manchester City Council as City Solicitor in 2018, taking up a role that shares services with Salford City Council – an agreement that has been in place since 2012 to share resources and reduces costs across the two city councils A respected member of the legal services profession, Fiona served as President of the Manchester Law Society in 2025, representing and supporting the legal community across the region Fiona will stand down as City Solicitor in May 2027. The process to find her replacement is now underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cllr Garry Bridges is set to be appointed as the new Leader of Manchester City Council at a special meeting this week (Thursday 3 September, 6pm) Cllr Bridges succeeds Cllr Bev Craig, who was elected as Greater Manchester Mayor in July, having previously served as statutory Deputy Leader since 2024. Subject to confirmation at the full Council meeting, he will take up the political leadership of the Council The Leader has ultimate responsibility for setting the long-term vision for the Council at the heart of Manchester’s ongoing inclusive growth, leading a team of Executive (Cabinet) members. He will represent the Council – and the city – at regional, national and international lev Cllr Bridges’ political priority has been ensuring that Manchester’s young people have the best start in life and have the opportunities, through work and skills, to share in the city’s success Prior to becoming Deputy Leader in 2024, Cllr Bridges had held the position of Executive Member for Children and Schools and overseen significant improvements across children’s services – which are now rated Outstanding by Ofsted. This included championing free school meals durin His commitment has been accentuated by his role as a parent to two toddlers, a daughter (aged three) and a son (aged four.)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Alejandro Garnacho Alejandro Garnacho suffers Champions League embarrassment as suspicions raised Former Manchester United star Alejandro Garnacho has struggled for regular minutes during his loan at Aston Villa - and things got even worse for him on Tuesday night Alejandro Garnacho was left rusting on the bench for Aston Villa's Champions League win on Tuesday night, leading to concerns the former Manchester United star could become the 'next Harvey Elliott'. Villa claimed a 3-2 victory over Club Brugge on Wednesday night, but Garnacho di Garnacho was named on the bench by Villa boss Unai Emery for the trip to Bruges, and remained an unused substitute throughout the game despite having played minutes in all their Premier League matches The Argentina international left United last year to join Chelsea in a deal worth £40million, and was loaned out to Villa this summer in a deal which could go on to be made permanent after his first season at Stamford Bridge didn't go according to plan However, Garnacho is yet to be handed a single start by Emery since making the move to Villa, and has had to settle for three late cameo appearances in each of the club’s Premier League fixtures, playing just 31 minutes so far this term After Villa’s win in Belgium, many of fans have expressed concern for Garnacho’s continued lack of minutes, with some referencing Elliott, who made just nine appearances during a torrid loan spell from Liverpool last season

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
